title: Failed Invocations and Suspended Instances are archived inside the Hub Data Repository instead of being deleted
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.2.1.1.4 spells out the routing for in-progress work: Invocations "that are completed successfully are moved to [the] Active Instances Directory, whereas failed Invocations are Archived in [the] Hub Data Repository."

That repository is subdivided for exactly this purpose. Under Archived Invocations/Instances sit two named slots: Failed Invocations (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.1.5.1.1) and Suspended Instances (A.6.1.1.4.2.1.1.1.5.1.2), each holding whole subtrees rather than summary records.

The non-obvious consequence is that the Artifact retains the ecosystem's failure history as a first-class part of its structure. An Agent cannot present a clean record by abandoning unsuccessful Invocations, because the destination for failure is defined in advance and lives in the same document tree as success. Each primitive therefore carries its own attempt log.

`Suspended` being an archive destination rather than an in-place status is also notable: suspension physically removes an Instance from the Active directory, so "what is currently active" stays literally true and cannot include dormant entries.
description: Invocation routing is explicit: success moves the subtree into the Active Instances Directory, failure moves it to archive — so attempts that never became Instances stay on the record.
